subject: Acme - Trial procurement & conversion readiness / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jared Bloom <jared.bloom@acme.com>
Cc: avery_johnson@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Acme - Trial procurement & conversion readiness / next steps

Hey Jared — great call this morning, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get your trial moving and make billing/conversion straightforward: 

Recap / asks from call:
- Trial goal: validate throughput on the 8k-context model for customer chat use case and reach 95th-pctl latency <200ms under typical load.
- Success criteria: >=100k tokens processed during pilot and resolution metrics improved by the CS team (we'll help instrument).
- Procurement path: you mentioned procurement prefers a PO but would like to evaluate AWS Marketplace pricing as well — can you confirm?

Next steps (proposal):
1) Please share your procurement contact + any standard procurement forms (I'll loop legal/ops).
2) We'll prepare a short SOW + pricing options: (A) credit card (fast, self-serve), (B) PO/net30 via SOW, (C) AWS Marketplace listing (may take extra lead time).
3) Confirm trial start/end dates and when you want billing to start (on conversion vs immediate pro-rated billing).

Attached: a quick procurement info template you can share with your procurement team so we capture PO fields we need.

If you can cc procurement@acme.com here we can start the paper path. I’ll loop in Dylan (SOW/pricing) and Avery (Marketplace / billing ops) to sync.

Thanks — I’ll aim to have a SOW draft by EOD tomorrow once you confirm procurement contact.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive
Redwood Inference
--Attachment: procurement-form.xlsx (xlsx, 14KB)

From: Jared Bloom <jared.bloom@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme - Trial procurement & conversion readiness / next steps

Thanks Marissa, appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers: 
- Procurement contact: procurement@acme.com (I’ve cc'd them).
- Preferred path: PO via SOW is our default for anything above $25k. We are open to Marketplace but will need a price parity check — if Marketplace pricing lines up, procurement may prefer that for easier billing.
- Trial success threshold: we typically sign off on trials when we hit a predefined usage floor (we're thinking ~100k tokens for this POC) AND technical acceptance (latency and error rate targets).

I attached a completed procurement form for your team to use. Also, please include a clear billing start recommendation in the SOW (we prefer to start billing on conversion date rather than automatically after trial, but happy to be explicit in the SOW).

Timeline: We can start the pilot the week of Nov 15 if SOW/PO move quickly. Can you confirm SOW turnaround and if Redwood can accept PO/net30?

Best,
Jared
Jared Bloom
Director, Platform Engineering | Acme Corp
--Attachment: acme-procurement-form-filled.xlsx (xlsx, 18KB)

Looping you both in — procurement (see cc) prefers PO via SOW, open to Marketplace if price parity checks out. Jared proposes a Nov 15 start.

Dylan: can you draft a 1-page SOW + 3 pricing options by EOD tomorrow? Items to include:
- Proposal to start billing on conversion date unless Acme requests pro-rated billing earlier.
- Payment terms: PO / net30 (confirm ops can accept).
- Reserved capacity discounts / committed throughput tiers (call out token thresholds).

Avery: can you check Marketplace listing ETA and whether we can offer price parity to match SOW/PO? If Marketplace won't be live by Nov 15, include that in the note.

Thanks — I’ll handle the outreach on instrumentation and trial success criteria with Jared's team.

—Marissa

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>

On Thu, Nov 5, 2026 at 10:25 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Looping you both in — procurement (see cc) prefers PO via SOW, open to Marketplace if price parity checks out. Jared proposes a Nov 15 start.

Thanks — I’ll put together a 1-page SOW and price options. Draft outline below:

SOW draft (summary):
- Scope: 30-day pilot for POC environment, up to 500k tokens included in pilot (overages billed monthly at listed rate unless otherwise agreed).
- Acceptance criteria: >=100k tokens and 95th-pctl latency <200ms under baseline traffic.
- Billing: Option A (Card/self-serve) — immediate billing on activation; Option B (PO/net30) — billing starts on conversion/acceptance; Option C (AWS Marketplace) — billing terms per marketplace rules (pricing parity required).
- Payment terms: Redwood accepts PO/net30 for enterprise customers; Ops to confirm billing contact for invoicing.

I attached a SOW PDF (draft) and a short pricing table with token bands and reserved discounts. Dylan (me) to coordinate with Legal for final language; should have a version for review by EOD tomorrow.

—Dylan
--Attachment: Redwood-SOW-draft.pdf (pdf, 46KB); Pricing-table.csv (csv, 6KB)

From: Jared Bloom <jared.bloom@acme.com>

Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme - Trial procurement & conversion readiness / next steps

Appreciate the fast turnaround — draft SOW looks good at a high level. A couple quick confirmations before we route to procurement/legal: 
- Trial window: Nov 15 - Dec 15 (30 days) works. We’ll aim to reach the 100k token threshold in that window; if we hit it earlier we can escalate.
- Acceptance: technical acceptance per SOW (95th-pctl latency <200ms) + usage floor.
- Billing: procurement prefers billing to start on conversion date (happy to sign PO once we accept results). Please include a clause that allows immediate billing if Acme requests production access before PO is issued.

If you can send the final SOW via DocuSign and include a line for "Billing start date: upon conversion unless customer requests earlier activation" we can route to procurement next week.
\I'll flag Marketplace interest with our finance team but for now let's proceed on the PO path to keep timelines tight.
\Thanks — Jared
